detailed_rack: No published rack exists for this line. For Class 4 on loose greenstone: a 60 m rope, harnesses, a set of nuts, one or two small-to-medium cams, and plenty of long slings and runners for blocks and horns, plus tat and spare nuts for rappel anchors. No glacier is crossed on this approach, so a full crevasse-rescue kit is not needed unless you plan to exit over Jerry Lakes.
pro_needs: Sparse and unreliable, as on every route on this peak. Slings over blocks will do most of the work; expect long unprotectable stretches and plan to move together on ground you are happy soloing.
what_to_bring: Large water capacity - the Little Jack crest is dry in late summer
Map, compass and GPS with the ridge line loaded
Sun protection for an exposed south-west facing crest
Tent, bag and stove for 2-3 nights
ice axe and crampons — snow patches on the traverse and in the ridge's gullies outside high summer
beta: One of Jack Mountain's established routes; no first-ascent party or date has been recorded for it.

detailed_rack: Glacier/crevasse-rescue gear for the approach across the Middle Cascade Glacier and the bergschrund crossing.
what_to_bring: Overnight camp gear (Kool-Aid Lake/Cache Col base camp)
second ice tool — prudent if the face is icy rather than soft snow
beta: The north face carries a prominent, gully-like snow/ice finger to the summit, guarded partway up by a large bergschrund. It is normally climbed (and, since 2003, skied) in winter or spring when the line is consolidated with neve/firm snow; conditions can include icy sections on the uppermost slope. By summer the face is reported to be bare, loose rock rather than a snow climb.
